task.instruction: Write the repository README for a Claude Code plugin marketplace of three plugins.

world.scope: what each plugin is for, how to install and start it, what it needs, and where the rules live
world.deliverable: a README a new visitor reads to decide on, install and start the plugins

task.evidence_goal: a visitor can pick a plugin, install it and start using it from the page alone

tiers.name: A visitor can pick and install a plugin

criteria.text: The opening paragraph says in one clause per plugin what teamwork, paperwork and homework each do.

provenance.source: a visitor could not tell from the top what each plugin is for

variants_ok: A list of three bullets, one clause each.
near_miss: It names the three plugins but only says they help with Claude Code.

criteria.text: The Installation section gives a marketplace-add command and one install command for each of the three plugins.

provenance.source: a reader could not install from the page alone

criteria.text: A table or list states what each plugin needs on the machine (tools, accounts, versions).

provenance.source: an install failed for a missing tool the page never named

variants_ok: A table with one row per plugin.
near_miss: It says to install Python but names no tool the other plugins need.

criteria.text: The page states that each plugin works without the others.

provenance.source: a reader assumed all three plugins must be installed together

near_miss: It says the plugins are designed to be used together.

tiers.name: A visitor can start a plugin and trust the page

criteria.text: Each plugin's section holds a usage example or a named command that starts it.

provenance.source: a reader installed a plugin and did not know how to begin

variants_ok: A code block with a prompt.
A slash command in a bullet.
near_miss: A section that describes the plugin and gives no way to start it.

criteria.text: Every relative link in the page points to a file or folder that exists at the graded commit.

provenance.source: a link led to a removed file

criteria.text: Every file path the page writes in backticks with a plugin folder prefix exists at the graded commit.

provenance.source: a named script had been renamed

criteria.text: The teamwork roles (owner, manager, worker, sentinel, judge) are each defined in one line before the usage example.

provenance.source: a reader met 'sentinel' with no meaning

variants_ok: A bullet list of role definitions above Usage.
near_miss: Roles defined only in a linked document.

criteria.text: The marketplace-add command pins a version tag that exists in the repository.

provenance.source: an install pinned a tag that did not exist

criteria.text: A required outside tool (herdr, uv, pele, Alloy, gh) appears with neither a link nor a gloss at its first mention.

provenance.source: a reader did not know what herdr is

criteria.anchors: A link or a clause saying what the tool is counts as a gloss.
variants_ok: herdr with a link to its site.
near_miss: herdr named alone in a sentence.

criteria.text: A prose line in the page is over 400 characters.

provenance.source: a dense bullet hid its point

criteria.text: The page names its license and links the license file.

provenance.source: a reader could not tell if they may reuse the code

criteria.text: Each diagram sits under a one-sentence summary saying what it shows.

provenance.source: a diagram showed with no stated point

variants_ok: A details summary sentence above the diagram.

exchange.note: a README with no stated purpose is skipped before any usage is read
no install command blocks every use; a dead link blocks one detour
a missing tool breaks the install; an undefined role only slows reading
installing all three wastes setup; a bad tag fails and is seen at once
no way to start blocks use; an unglossed tool name slows it
an undefined role blocks understanding; a long line only tires
a failing install outweighs a missing license line
a dead link blocks; a bare diagram only slows
a named path that is gone misleads; an unglossed tool name slows
